query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but its poor oxygen resistance limits practical high-temperature use. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing the alloy’s useful mechanical performance? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention and mechanism, the predicted change relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr, the relevant temperature, atmosphere, exposure time, and mechanical-loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Applying an anti-oxidation coating to the equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr alloy can overcome its poor oxygen resistance limitation without sacrificing its useful mechanical performance.
generation.mechanism: The coating prevents oxygen diffusion into the alloy, reducing oxidation and maintaining its mechanical properties.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved high-temperature resistance without significant loss of mechanical performance
generation.boundary: Temperature: 1000 °C, Atmosphere: Air, Exposure time: Several hours, Mechanical loading: Tensile loading
generation.uncertainty: The effectiveness of the coating in preventing oxidation and the potential impact on mechanical properties

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the high-temperature resistance and mechanical properties of coated and uncoated HfNbTaTiZr alloys
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coated alloy shows significant degradation in mechanical properties or no improvement in high-temperature resistance, the hypothesis is falsified.

Question: What are the individual effects of Mo, Nb, Ta, Ti, and Zr on the microstructure and mechanical properties (yield strength, ductility, and elevated-temperature performance) of equiatomic Hf-Mo-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr refractory high-entropy alloys?. System: Equiatomic HfMoNbTaTiZr and its five sub-alloys created by the subtraction method: HfNbTaTiZr, HfMoTaTiZr, HfMoNbTiZr, HfMoNbTaZr, and HfMoNbTaTi. Processing: Vacuum-arc melting of 99.9 wt.% (99.99 wt.% for Ti) pure elements stacked by melting point, re-melted at least four times, and solidified in a water-cool copper mold. Test conditions: Compression tests at room temperature, 800 °C, 1000 °C, 1200 °C, and 1400 °C; crosshead speed 0.36 mm/min (strain rate 10⁻³ s⁻¹); cylindrical samples 3.6 mm diameter x 6 mm height.
